name: CCTV-Smartphone-AI-Monitoring
description: 本地监控 + AI 视觉 — LAN-based smartphone-powered AI monitoring framework with structured event output for data acquisition and analysis.
readme_summary: Sentinel is a distributed real-time vision system framework for local area networks (LAN) that repurposes unused Android devices as network camera nodes. It enables distributed image acquisition, real-time PC-side video streaming, and AI-driven monitoring and analysis, supporting local video recording and structured event output.
key_features: Repurposes Android devices as network camera nodes
Layered architecture: mobile capture + PC processing + browser control
primary_use_case: To create a distributed, AI-powered local monitoring system by repurposing old Android smartphones as cameras, with a PC dashboard for control and analysis.
cover_image_prompt: A wise old owl perched on a network server rack, its eyes glowing with digital data streams. The owl is holding a smartphone in its talons, which is projecting a live video feed onto a large screen displaying various AI-analyzed events like 'person detected' and 'object moved'. The background is a dimly lit, organized server room with subtle circuit board patterns. Small, glowing icons representing data packets and AI analysis float around the scene. The repository name 'Sentinel' is subtly etched on the owl's perch. The overall mood is vigilant and intelligent. Style: 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clear iconography and a cool, tech-inspired color palette.

name: Phosphor
description: Free and open-source iOS device manager for macOS. Browse backups, export messages, extract photos, manage apps - no subscriptions, no iCloud lock-in.
readme_summary: Phosphor is a free, open-source iOS device manager for macOS that allows users to manage their iPhones, iPads, and iPods without relying on Apple's proprietary software or iCloud. It offers comprehensive control over device backups, data extraction, app management, and diagnostics.
primary_use_case: Managing and accessing data from iOS devices on macOS without proprietary software or subscriptions.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled librarian in a vast, organized archive, meticulously cataloging and retrieving diverse items from old, leather-bound books (representing iOS device backups). The librarian uses a magnifying glass that reveals digital data streams and icons (photos, messages, apps) flowing from the books. In the background, a sleek macOS interface is subtly visible, displaying the librarian's actions. The overall mood is one of control, accessibility, and freedom from digital clutter. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with a clean, modern aesthetic and a color palette emphasizing blues, greens, and subtle metallic accents, with the 'Phosphor' name subtly integrated into a library sign.

name: apkleaks
description: Scanning APK file for URIs, endpoints & secrets.
readme_summary: APKleaks is a Python-based tool designed for static analysis of Android APK files. It scans these files to identify URIs, network endpoints, and sensitive secrets, aiding in security assessments and bug bounty hunting.
key_features: Scans APK files for URIs, endpoints, and secrets
Supports installation via PyPI, from source, and Docker
Allows custom pattern definitions using JSON for targeted scanning
Integrates with the JADX decompiler for deeper analysis
Provides options for output formatting (text, JSON) and file redirection
primary_use_case: Static analysis of Android APK files to discover sensitive information like URIs, endpoints, and secrets for security auditing and bug bounty hunting.
cover_image_prompt: A digital detective, wearing a futuristic visor, meticulously sifting through the intricate gears and circuits of a giant, transparent Android robot. Glowing lines of code and data streams flow from the robot's core, with the detective highlighting suspicious fragments that glow red. Small, holographic screens around the detective display discovered URIs and potential secrets. The scene is set in a dimly lit, high-tech workshop, with the Android robot as the central focus. The overall mood is one of intense scrutiny and discovery. The image should be in a 3D isometric illustration style, emphasizing clarity and detail, with a color palette of blues, purples, and glowing red accents.

name: floccus
description: :cloud: Sync your bookmarks privately across browsers and devices
readme_summary: Floccus is a browser extension and mobile app designed to synchronize bookmarks privately across various browsers and devices. It supports multiple cloud storage providers and offers customizable sync strategies, intervals, and folder selections.
key_features: Supports sync via Nextcloud Bookmarks, Linkwarden, KaraKeep, Google Drive, Dropbox, Git servers, and WebDAV
Compatible with browsers supporting Web extensions (Firefox, Chrome, Edge, etc.)
Offers a mobile app for Android/iOS
Allows creation of multiple sync profiles
Provides control over sync strategy (uni- or bidirectional), interval, and folder
primary_use_case: Synchronizing bookmarks privately across different browsers and devices using a user-chosen cloud storage service.
cover_image_prompt: A whimsical, anthropomorphic bookmark character with a determined expression, holding a glowing digital thread. This thread connects to multiple diverse browser icons (Firefox, Chrome, Edge) and cloud service icons (Nextcloud, Dropbox, Git). The bookmark character is actively weaving these threads together, creating a seamless, unified stream of bookmark data flowing from the browsers to the clouds. Subtle digital particles and data streams flow along the threads, indicating the synchronization process. The scene is set against a clean, abstract background with a soft, inviting glow, emphasizing privacy and ease of use. The overall style is a friendly, 3D isometric illustration with clear iconography and a vibrant, harmonious color palette, making the concept of cross-browser bookmark sync instantly understandable.
